newsitem.title: BELGIUM: FOCUS-EU to tell Belgium to scrap VTM ad monopoly.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-EU to tell Belgium to scrap VTM ad monopoly.

text.p: The European Commission will tell Belgium on Thursday to scrap the advertising monopoly granted to commercial TV channel VTM for the Flanders region.

Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert said the Commission would agree at its weekly meeting that the monopoly was illegal, rejecting the argument by the Flanders government that it was intended to safeguard the pluralism of the press.
VTM's 18-year monopoly for the Dutch-speaking northern Belgian region of Flanders, granted in 1989, has been attacked by rival VT4.
VT4, owned by Nasdaq-listed TV group Scandinavian Broadcasting System, has been broadcasting from London to Flanders to circumvent the monopoly.

VTM, 44 percent owned by Dutch publishing group VNU , said on Wednesday it would claim 15 to 20 billion francs ($421 to $562 million) in damages from the Flemish government if it lost its advertising monopoly.
Flemish Economic Affairs and Media Minister Eric Van Rompuy said on Thursday it would reject any such claim.

"If the European Commission declares us in default today, we'll have to lift the monopoly... and adjust our laws. So I don't really see how there could be a claim for damages," he told Belgian BRTN radio.
Explaining the expected decision to reporters, Van Miert also said VTM would have no legal grounds to seek compensation.
"I don't see how on a solid basis one could ask compensation," he said. He suggested that VTM be satisfied that it enjoyed a monopoly for such a long time.
The Flemish government long resisted abolishing VTM's exclusive rights arguing that the channel's advertising revenue is distributed among the region's written press which owns VTM.

Van Miert noted that VTM is presently controlled by three media groups against an initial nine and this weakened the press pluralism argument. He also said that the monopoly could be justified on "general good" reasons.
Besides VNU, VTM is controlled by Persgroep NV and Roularta Mediagroep.
The Belgian authorities have two months to comply with the decision or face legal action.
-- Amelia Torres Brussels Newsroom +32 2 2876841 ($ = 35.6 Belgian Francs)
